lines.text: Tinplate, Indiana. Pop. 1,204. Home of a water tower shaped like a spark plug.
WTPL 1340, the Voice of Tinplate! Walt Pickering here with your noon news.
Augie Moss, who fixed every mower in the county, has left his shed to kin.
And the Crownwell family wants it. They want everything. Back after this.
A shed. Two wrenches. One raccoon. And a note: DON'T SELL TO THE CROWNWELLS.
So you're Augie's kin. You've got his chin. Let's hope you've got his ears.
Hazel Pruitt. Call me Jets. I've rejetted more carbs than you've had birthdays.
Augie and I raced together for forty years. Mostly against the Crownwells.
So. You gonna sell to them like the rest of this town did?

reply.text: Ha! Augie's chin AND Augie's mouth. Good.
Wrong answer, but honest. Augie would've laughed. Then thrown a wrench.

lines.text: Um. Hi. I'm Dewey Brandt. I fix tractors. Your raccoon is in the carburetor.
Dewey can fix anything with an engine. He can't talk to anything with a face.
That's... fair.
Rosie Alvarez, Sal's Pizza! Thirty minutes or it's free. Never once been free.
Heard you need a driver. I got a moped, a temper and zero fear. Hire me.
First, build a machine. Body, layout, carbs. Dewey will turn the wrenches.
Race it, win something. Then we'll talk about a real garage.
It runs! It RUNS! ...Mostly. The raccoon moved out, anyway.
Lesson one, kid. Rich runs slow and safe. Lean runs fast and hot.
Too lean and you'll put a hole in a piston. I've seen it. I've DONE it.
Jets meter the fuel. Bigger jet, richer mix. One size at a time. Always.
Can I drive it yet? I'll be gentle. I'm lying, but I'll try.
WTPL here! The Moss shed has raced! Folks, the shed RACED!
Cute lawnmower. Did your uncle leave you the grass too?
Who's the haircut?
Preston Crownwell. His mom owns seven car lots, the bank and half the fair.
Crownwell has won the county fair 22 years running. Enjoy the view, Shed Kid.
That boy's never turned a wrench in his life. Rosie, eat his lunch next time.
Oh, I'm eating his lunch AND his dessert.
A WIN for the Moss shed! I nearly dropped my sandwich, folks!
Hon! Barb Dunleavy, Corn Belt Oil! Keeping engines slick since forever!
We sponsor winners. And folks who might win. And the pie booth.
How about it, hon? Our logo on your fender, a little cash up front?

reply.text: That's what I like! Here's a signing bonus. It was in my purse.
The catch is you wear a corn hat in the fair parade. Very flattering.

lines.text: Sign her in the Sponsors menu, kid. Corn Belt's good people.
Rookie champions! From a shed! This is going on the Clarion's front page!
So this is Augie's little shed. How quaint. Victoria Crownwell.
Cute trophy. Preston won one just like it. When he was nine.
Let's be adults. I'll buy the shed, the name and the raccoon. Name a price.

reply.text: Everything is for sale, dear. Some things just haven't heard the price.
...Charming. I'll ask again once you've lost something.

lines.text: Forty years she's tried to buy Augie out. Forty years he said no.
The old Feed & Seed on Main Street. Four bays, one roof, zero raccoons.
A real lift! A parts washer! I might cry. I'm not gonna cry. I'm crying.
Rookie champs, baby! Next stop: the Nationals!
Don't get cocky. National cars run faster, and the air don't care who you are.
WTPL Sports. The Tinplate team moves up to National racing this season.
Back in my day we read spark plugs like tea leaves. Tan's good. Black's rich.
White means you're about to buy a piston. Don't make white.
Research a wideband O2 sensor. It reads the mix live. Don't tell Augie.
He's... not around to tell, Hazel.
I know, son. I still talk to him. He still doesn't listen.
Big ones this year: Thunder Valley, Snowbound, Monsoon Mile, the Half-Mile!
The wideband's in! It reads air-fuel ratio. Like, live. Like magic.
Not magic. Math. About 12.8 to 1 at full throttle, near 14.7 cruising.
Rich at idle's fine. Lean at wide open is how engines die young.
...Fine. It's a little bit magic.
Boss. Got a sec? Preston offered me a seat. Crownwell factory car. Real money.
Pizza never paid like this. My mom could finally fix her roof.
So... what do you think?

reply.text: ...Huh. Nobody ever said that to me before. Lemme think on it.
Need, huh? ...Okay. That's a good word. Lemme think on it.

lines.text: Crownwell buys drivers like they buy car lots. Doesn't mean they keep 'em.
NATIONAL CHAMPIONS! The Feed & Seed crew did it, folks!
Boss. I told Preston no. I'm a Tinplate driver. Pizza's still on me, though.
You let me choose. That's why I'm staying.
You said you needed me. Turns out I needed to hear it.
You turned down CROWNWELL? For a feed store?
It's a garage now. Keep up, haircut.
The old Starlite Drive-In. The big screen makes a heck of a billboard.
Six bays. A dyno room. We can watch movies on the screen at night!
Continental racing next. Different countries, different air.
And kid... it's time we talked about fuel injection.
YES!
Don't 'yes' me. I'm still mad about it.
WTPL World Desk! Which is my desk, turned to face the window.
Fuel injection. Computers telling engines what to drink. Augie'd be sick.
Augie bought a laptop in 2009, Hazel. I found it under the raccoon nest.
...Traitor.
EFI is a carb made of numbers. A VE table. Every cell is a little jet.
Every cell's a jet? ...Huh. Okay. Say more.
Research throttle-body EFI. Then build a machine on it, or convert one.
You're the Tinplate team. Silas Vane. They call me the Silver Fox.
Your driver brakes late. Good. She'll learn to brake later.
Was that a compliment or a threat?
Yes.
Silas Vane, folks. Three world titles. Never smiles. Except just now. Brr.
So this is a VE table. Rows are load, columns are RPM. Each one's a jet.
Rejet only 4,000 RPM at full load and leave idle alone? ...Oh my.
Told you!
Don't. Gimme the laptop. And coffee. And don't talk to me for an hour.
EFI's live! Base map loaded! She fired on the first crank!
Idles like a sewing machine. Augie, you old goat. You were right.
Does it go faster?
It goes smarter. Faster is your job. Go tune the map.
Live on WTPL: Tinplate mechanic Dewey Brandt! Dewey, what's the secret?
I, uh. Um. The, uh... secret is...
Breathe, son. Talk to him like he's a tractor.
...It's not magic. It's float height. And honest welds. And Hazel.
Float height, folks! Write that down! I'm writing it down!
I did a radio! I DID A RADIO!
The old Tinplate Can Company. The town made tin cans here for ninety years.
Now it makes race machines. Half the town showed up to sweep the floors.
Hon, it's beautiful! I brought a casserole! And a camera crew!
World tier, kid. Crownwell's home turf. Let's go mess it up.
Tinplate goes WORLD! Population 1,204. Fans? A whole lot more!
Congratulations. You've become expensive. That's why I'm here.
My final offer. The factory, the team, the name. Everyone has a number.

reply.text: Zero. How very small town of you.
A wager? Oh, I like you. Win on the world stage first. Then we'll talk.

lines.text: Same offer, different hat. Forty years of it.
Win on the world stage, kid. Make them say Tinplate on foreign TV.
Hey. Shed Kid. ...Your crew actually likes you, huh?
Mother hired my crew. Mother hired my friends. Mother hired my dog trainer.
...You okay, haircut?
I'm FINE. Forget I said anything. Crownwells don't lose. Or talk.
A WORLD WIN! Tinplate, Indiana, folks! Look it up! It's on maps now!
Clean race. You'll want to do that again when it matters.
The Crownwell Cup. She's going to ask you. Say yes.
Very well. The Crownwell Cup. You, me, my best machine, my best driver.
Win, and I'll never make another offer. Lose, and you sell me the factory.
She's betting the factory on one race?
...Good. Augie lost the Cup in '79 by a nose. We owe him a nose.
I got a nose for this.
That's not how noses work.
Cup week. Tinplate closes the schools. The diner names a pie after Rosie.
Boss. I built something. Hazel helped. Okay, Hazel yelled and I built.
Augie's notes, Hazel's jetting, my welds. We call it the Tinplate Special.
And my cam timing. Victoria never let me try it. Her loss.
Machines don't win races. People who build machines win races.
Build her up, tune her right, and beat Silas Vane. Simple.
I look forward to it. Truly. Bring everything you have.
The grid is set. Crownwell Racing has never lost the Cup. Not once.
Close. Closer than anyone in years. Again?
Again. Rejet, rethink, rerun. We go AGAIN.
THEY DID IT! TINPLATE WINS THE CROWNWELL CUP! I'm standing on my desk!
Well driven. Nine years since I lost a race I wanted. Thank you.
Mother's furious. Best day of my life. Next year, Shed Kid.
...A deal is a deal. No more offers.
Augie Moss would have been insufferable about this. Well raced.
We got him his nose, kid. After all these years. We got him his nose.
